# Progress

A bar that shows how far along a task is, or that it is under way when you can't tell. It is a labeled `progressbar`, so screen readers hear the label and the value.

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/progress/progress";
```

## Example

```tsx
<Progress label="Uploading photos" value={40} showValue />
<Progress label="Importing recipes" value={null} />
```

## Use instead when

- Use `Spinner` instead for a short wait with no measurable progress, and `Skeleton` to hold the place of content that is loading.

## Props

Type: `ProgressProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement (`mt-4`, `max-w-sm`). Appearance classes warn in development; use `tone`. |
| `format` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` |  | How the value is written, for `showValue` and screen readers: `{ style: "unit", unit: "megabyte" }`. |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` |  | Hides the label visually; screen readers still use it. |
| `id` | `string` |  | The progress bar's id, for `aria-describedby` or `aria-controls` elsewhere on the page. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What is in progress: "Uploading photos". It names the bar for screen readers. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | The value at the end of the bar, when the work is done. |
| `min` | `number` | `0` | The value at the start of the bar. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` |  | Shows the value beside the label, as a percentage unless `format` says otherwise. |
| `tone` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "destructive" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `"primary"` | Color role from the theme for the filled part, named after its token. `secondary` is the muted foreground. |
| `value` (required) | `number \| null` |  | How far along the work is, from `min` to `max`. `null` while you don't know: the bar is indeterminate and slides instead of filling. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `color`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `tone`: `<Progress tone="success">`.
- `indeterminate`: Not a prop. An unknown value is `null`: `<Progress value={null}>`.
- `isIndeterminate`: Not a prop. An unknown value is `null`: `<Progress value={null}>`.
- `variant`: Not a prop. A number `value` is determinate, `null` indeterminate.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: each component merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with the component's own replaces it.

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.
